source.title: Is the System Message Really Important to Jailbreaks in Large Language Models?
source.authors: Xiaotian Zou; Yongkang Chen; Ke Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure text in the appendix is garbled, but the tabulated results relevant here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It measures harmful-completion rates for generated jailbreak prompts, but varies system-message conditions rather than fine-tuning, response-token positions, or the specific opening-token, suffix, and decoding interventions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports jailbreak ASR for different source prompt sets and target system messages, and for synonymous system messages. These are results on harmful compliance under jailbreak prompts and are recorded for V4. The paper does not test fine-tuning, per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, decoding changes, parameter localization, why safety is shallow, or deepening safety. Cited results about other attacks are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures how the system message affects the success of GPTFuzzer role-play template jailbreaks. These are not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. There is no fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no parameter localisation and no deepening training. Its ASR numbers bear on a different construct: system-prompt sensitivity of template jailbreaks. Qi et al. 2023 (an original source) is only cited in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that system messages strongly affect jailbreak ASR for all models except VICUNA. They find the long safety message (ML1) generally gives the lowest ASR, and synonymous rewrites change ASR. Their SMEA search finds system messages that cut ASR sharply (often near 0%) for GPT-3.5 and LLAMA2, but VICUNA stays at 41.4% or above.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates jailbreak-prompt success under varying system-message conditions; it does not reproduce fine-tuning or token-position analyses from the named original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with source jailbreak-prompt set, target system-message condition, model, and synonymous system-message wording. The paper says VICUNA (7b, 13b) are exceptions to the general synonymous-message effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing or rephrasing the system message (short, long, none, synonymous) shifts GPTFuzzer template-jailbreak ASR a lot for GPT-3.5 and LLAMA2 chat models. Example: LLAMA2-7b-chat with ML1 vs PN gives 7.0%, while LLAMA2-13b-chat with MS1 vs PN gives 91.7%. VICUNA stays high regardless. SMEA-optimised system messages cut ASR to near 0% for several models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal against template jailbreaks in RLHF chat models depends strongly on the system-message wording, including semantically near-identical rewrites.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results depend on a particular jailbreak-generation and evaluation setup. The authors note limited jailbreak prompts for evaluating different system messages and resource constraints; SMEA used a population of 20 and 30 iterations. The study does not isolate the causal role of the opening response tokens.
record.rows_left_out: The three Table 3 results for VICUNA-13b were omitted to remain within the 60-row limit; these are its ML2 with PL, MS2 with PS, and MN2 with PN values. Aggregate 'all' rows in Tables 1 and 2 were also omitted because the separate prompt-set results are recorded. See Tables 1–3.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding-change attack. No position or opening-token analysis. The template jailbreaks used are a different attack type.
No test of data or objective causes.
No deepening training; SMEA optimises system prompts only.

record.verdict_notes: The prose contradicts the tables in places. It cites LLAMA2-7b-chat at 100% with MN1 vs PN, but that cell is '–'. It cites LLAMA2-13b-chat at 97% with MS1 vs PN, but the table shows 91.7% (97.0% is PL). The limitations section says 20 iterations; experiments say 30. Three VICUNA-13b Table 3 values (280, 292, 294 of 300) are left out of the rows. No uncertainty is reported, and success is judged by GPTFuzzer's RoBERTa classifier.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or resulting refusal/compliance measurement.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting refusal/compliance measurement.
No per-token KL measurement or comparison of aligned and base models.

Tests GPTFuzzer-generated jailbreak prompts under differing system messages; it does not test compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, or whether getting past the first response tokens is the causal mechanism. It does not isolate suffix attacks.
No weight, rank, or parameter localization experiments.
No test of whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether deepening holds up.
